 Proposed rule could cut SNAP benefits for 6.3 million Americans 
 Proposal could cut SNAP benefits By KPLC Digital Team and Karringtan Harris Published : Nov. 12, 2026 at 3:21 PM CST | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LAKE CHARLES, La. (KPLC) - The Trump administration proposed a rule that could cut food stamp benefits for 6.3 million people.
 The U.S. Department of Agriculture proposal , released Monday, would limit automatic eligibility for SNAP to low-income households that receive cash assistance through the TANF program.
 Households receiving noncash or nominal TANF services would no longer automatically qualify for SNAP under the proposal.
 According to the proposal, the change would save $44.6 billion between 2027 and 2031. It is the Trump administration’s latest effort to curb SNAP spending, citing concerns about waste and fraud.
 The proposal targets a policy known as “broad-based categorical eligibility,” which allows states to use TANF benefits such as child care or workforce training to qualify households for SNAP without applying the program’s standard income eligibility limit.
 The changes would make SNAP eligibility more standardized and “preserve benefits for the truly needy,” the rule said.
 United Way of Southwest Louisiana says the change could weigh on families.
 “We look at ALICE, which is the acronym for Asset Limited and Income Constrained, but Employed. So those working folks that are just barely making ends meet will also be affected by this,” said Laurie Martin, vice president of community impact for United Way of Southwest Louisiana.
 “They will have to make some tough decisions. They’ll have to make decisions on whether their child can play an extracurricular sport and having to buy those uniforms instead of having to put food on the table,” Martin said.
 Martin also expects more people to seek help from United Way.
 “Well, the changes are going to affect us here at United Way and the amount of referrals that we’ll be getting. And giving. So we have the 2-1-1 call center. So we expect that the calls to increase for people needing assistance with food,” she said.
 Dr. Steven Procopio, president of the Public Affairs Research Council of Louisiana, said the proposal raises a question about the trade-off between saving money and food insecurity.
 “Is the money saved going to be worth the additional food insecurity that will happen? And that is a judgment call,” Procopio said.
 The USDA also estimates that 1.8 million children would also lose eligibility for free school lunches under the proposed rule.
 Nearly 18% of SNAP recipients, or about 6.3 million people, would lose benefits under the change.
 Officials with the United Way of Southwest Louisiana said they expect calls for assistance to increase if the proposal is approved.
 The public will have 30 days to comment on the proposed rule. Written comments must be received on or before Dec. 10 by the following methods:
 Online at regulations.gov 
 Mail comments to SNAP Program Development Division, Food and Nutrition Administration, 5601 Sunnyside Ave., Beltsville, MD 20705 
 Email comments to sm.fn.snappdbrules@usda.gov . Include Docket ID Number [FNA-2026-0661], “Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility” in the subject line of the message.
